learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialty, at a level that allows acquiring the rest of the degree's competencies.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply relevant analytical, calculation, and experimental methods already established and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in their field of specialty.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in a team, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Models and solves geometric, physical, and engineering problems using differential equations.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithmics; statistics and optimization.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.

Be able to identify their own training needs in their field of study and work or professional environment and to organize their own learning with a high degree of autonomy in all types of contexts (structured or unstructured).

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
That students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

syllabus_topics: Linear Algebra: Systems of linear equations
Linear Algebra: Inner product, norm and orthogonality
teaching_methods: Professor's presentation in participatory classes of concepts and procedures
Computer simulation practices, individually and/or in teams
Development, writing, and presentation of reports, audiovisual material related to projects/POPBLs

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation delivered, presentation and technical defense

assessment_rules: Recovery for written and oral tests is available. The final grade for checkpoints involves a written recovery (75%) and the checkpoint score (25%). Practices and self-assessments will be recovered through continuous assessment. For specific learning outcomes, such as RGM114, evaluation consists of two written tests (30% and 70% weight respectively), with recovery for a single test.
